_comment: Scenarios for src/api/login.js: login() is run against a fake panel and must resolve to expected.zoneTuples or reject with expected.error (exact message). Unless a row says otherwise the panel behaves like mock_paradox.ts with session value 91AC25D06A0C26BA, accepts the u/p of crypto.json 'sample session, 4 digit code' (username user, password 1234) and lists the six sample zones. 'panel' overrides the answer for one request path: a response or a list of responses used in order; each response is {file} (relative to tests/), {body}, {status[, headers][, body]} (200, no extra headers and an empty body when omitted), {zones} (the index page with these [area bitmask, name] slots, padded to 32 slots with [0, ' '] like the real panel), {zones_by_slot} (the same, sparse: slot index -> [area bitmask, name]), {destroy} (the connection is reset) or {hang} (never answered); 'times' limits how often a response is used (forever when omitted). 'expected.default_query' is the exact query string of the first /default.html request. 'expected.request_counts' is how often the panel was asked for each path (a path that is not listed was never asked; one request to each of /logout.html, /login_page.html, /default.html and /index.html when the whole object is omitted). A login that fails after the panel accepted the credentials logs out again, so such rows count two /logout.html requests. 'expected.warnings' are the messages logged with console.warn (none when omitted). index_retry rows run on a fake clock: 'expected.index_at_ms' is when each /index.html request is made, in ms from the first one; a request may not come a millisecond earlier, and login() settles right after the last one without waiting further. hangs rows run on a fake clock too, against a panel that leaves some requests unanswered: each of them fails 10000 ms after it was sent. Their 'expected.requests' lists every request the panel receives, in order, as [ms after login() was called, path], and 'expected.settles_at_ms' is when login() settles; neither may come a millisecond earlier. Error messages starting with 'Request failed' come from axios and 'socket hang up' / 'connect ECONNREFUSED' from Node's http client: a port only has to fail there. 'timeout of 10000ms exceeded' is the bridge's own.
